boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Port Hudson record (May 21-July 9, 1863) in Siege of Port Hudson [May-July 1863]. Plains Store on May 21 is recorded separately (LA009) and its losses are not counted here. The investment of May 22-25, the Clinton expedition, Logan's raids, Springfield Landing and the June operations against Taylor are context; siege-wide totals are not assigned to Plains Store or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads XIX Army Corps, Army of the Gulf [US] and the Confederate forces of the 3rd District at Port Hudson [CS]; the live field reads zero. Irwin says Gardner held the place with about seven thousand of all arms after the garrison of 16,287 present for duty at the end of March had been drawn on for Vicksburg; that the besiegers outnumbered the garrison rather more than two to one on May 26; that the besiegers' effective strength never exceeded 17,000, with less than 12,000 available for the siege and hardly 8,000 effective outside the cavalry at the end; and that 6,340 prisoners were taken. His footnote says the May and June returns only carry March forward. Miles says on July 6 that he had less than 400 muskets for over a mile and a half of breastworks.
claims.rationale: Figures for different dates, bases and scopes from a history and an interested report; the prisoner count is a post-surrender figure and not an opening strength. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 12,208 total (US 5,000; CS 7,208); the live field reads 17500 total (US 10000; CS 7500). Irwin gives Union losses of 1,995 on May 27, 1,805 on June 14 and 4,363 for the siege, and says at least as many more were sick. He cites a partial undated Confederate surgeon's return of 176 killed and 447 wounded (623), excluding Plains Store, and Jackson's report of 200 killed, 300-400 wounded and 200 dead of sickness; Beall's brigade lost 358 to June 1. Miles reports 4 killed and 11 wounded on his line on June 14. The garrison surrendered 6,340 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen and live totals differ widely and appear to include the surrendered garrison; their basis is not stated. Sick are not battle casualties.

open_questions: Banks's No. 1 siege reports, the Union returns (No. 2), the signal officers' and brigade reports (Nos. 3-31), Gardner's report (not found in the inspected list), Jackson's No. 33 report and the No. 34 returns, Beall's, Steedman's and the other Confederate reports (Nos. 35-48), the naval reports and Irwin's appendix loss tables remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892), already registered for the Red River pass, is an interested Union history by the corps' assistant adjutant-general. Irwin served on Banks's staff during the siege and was named a surrender commissioner, and his chapters cite Miles's report and a Confederate surgeon's partial return, so they are not independent of them. Miles's May 22 report and May 24-July 7 field reports (Official Records Series I, Volume XXVI, Part 1, a shared container) are one interested Confederate family; Miles commanded a legion and later the right wing, not the garrison. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
